newsitem.title: GERMANY: VW plans in-house agency for temp workers - report.
newsitem.headline: VW plans in-house agency for temp workers - report.

text.p: German carmaker Volkswagen AG hopes to establish an in-house employment agency for temporary workers, enabling it to lower wage costs, a German newspaper reported on Wednesday.
According to the Hannoversche Allgemeine Zeitung, staff managed by the internal agency would be paid according to the industry-wide wage agreement, rather than the more expensive VW wage package.

Volkswagen replied to the report in a statement, saying the proposal was part of current wage talks, but it declined to comment on any aspect of the wage talks before a next round of negotiations on April 17.

Sources at union IG Metall said the scheme would create a total of 800 to 1,000 new jobs at plants in Hannover, Emden and Kassel, but said temporary staff would create problems because workers performing the same tasks would be paid differently.

If true, the report would be the latest attempt by Volkswagen to reduce its wage costs. VW employees are paid four to five marks ($2.40 to $3.00) an hour more than their counterparts at other engineering companies in the state of Lower Saxony.
Volkswagen, Europe's largest carmaker, has in the past tried many ways to make its workforce more flexible so that production could be increased during periods of heavy demand.

The carmaker faces a difficult task in keeping labour costs down because the state government, which owns a 20 percent share in VW, has opposed some attempts by VW to reduce its workforce as other German carmakers have.
The carmaker and unions have met twice to agree a new wage contract, agreeing on March 26 to hold a third round of talks on April 17.
